macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats amid renewed U.S.-Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher after oil prices steadied, even as markets weighed the impact of fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and the risk that the conflict could worsen. Reuters also reported broader risk-on/risk-off moves in Europe and Asia, with oil, the dollar, and bonds reacting to the geopolitical shock.

items.title: European shares rise in choppy trade as investors weigh Middle East conflict
items.summary: European equities recovered modestly, led by technology stocks, while traders monitored the potential economic and inflation impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict. Reuters said oil prices and safe-haven flows continued to influence equity, currency, and bond markets.

items.title: Oil surge drives inflation fears, bond selling, and stronger dollar
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil prices rose after fresh U.S. strikes against Iran, reviving concerns about inflation and the risk of broader market disruption. The dollar held firm as investors sought safety, and longer-dated Japanese government bond yields hit a 30-year high.

items.title: Fed caution weighs on Asian and Australian markets
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Australian shares wobbled as Federal Reserve caution tempered the boost from lower oil prices. The same market snapshot showed mixed performance across regional assets, including a firming in some commodity-linked markets.

items.title: ECB minutes show policymakers still worried about inflation staying above target
items.summary: Reuters reported that European Central Bank accounts from the prior meeting showed policymakers were presented with projections that inflation would stay above target into next year despite nearly three expected rate hikes. The minutes reinforce the view that rate cuts are not imminent if inflation proves sticky.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 world growth forecast on Iran war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 global growth forecast to 3 percent, citing fallout from the Iran war. The forecast revision reflects the economic drag from higher energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Travel stocks fall as Brent crude jumps to two-week high
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that renewed fighting sent Brent crude above $76 a barrel, pressuring airlines and travel-related stocks while energy shares rallied. United Airlines was cited among the companies that sold off as fuel-cost concerns rose.

items.title: AstraZeneca disappoints in late-stage trial, weighing on the FTSE 100
items.summary: Reuters said the FTSE 100 slipped as investors digested renewed Middle East tensions and weaker-than-expected trial results from AstraZeneca. The company-specific setback added to broader risk aversion in UK equities.

items.title: Bank of America extends $520 million credit line to OpenAI
items.summary: Reuters reported that Bank of America provided OpenAI with a $520 million credit line, marking its first loan to the AI company as it prepares for a potential IPO. The move underscores continued lender interest in AI-related firms.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain shared ledger with Citi and HSBC
items.summary: Reuters reported that Swift launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC, to enable around-the-clock payments. The initiative is part of the payments network's push to compete with stablecoin infrastructure.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto markets slip as Bitcoin and Ethereum pause recovery
items.summary: Bitcoin fell back to around $62,700-$65,400 and Ethereum slipped toward $1,800-$1,950, while the broader crypto market stayed near $2.24 trillion. The day’s strongest large-cap movers included Hedera, Uniswap, and Aptos, while Filecoin, Stellar, and Bitcoin Cash declined.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins fall as Middle East tensions weigh on risk assets
items.summary: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin dropped as elevated Middle East tensions and US strikes on Iran reduced investor risk appetite. The move reversed some earlier weekly gains in the largest cryptocurrencies.

items.title: Coinbase Premium breakdown and whale activity push Bitcoin toward $64K
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly rallied to about $64,000 as whale activity and a shift in the Coinbase Premium were cited as market drivers. The move highlights continued sensitivity to large-holder flows and exchange-side demand signals.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong’s SFC ordered crypto platforms to move away from SMS authentication, signaling another step in the city’s push for stronger exchange security standards. The change affects operational compliance for licensed crypto businesses in the jurisdiction.

items.title: Paul Grewal exits Coinbase legal role ahead of key CLARITY vote
items.summary: Coinbase’s legal leadership change comes as US lawmakers approach a pivotal vote on crypto market structure legislation. The timing adds attention to regulatory lobbying and the industry’s push for clearer rules.

items.title: BlackRock moves $256.8 million in BTC and ETH to Coinbase
items.summary: Odaily reported that BlackRock deposited a large amount of Bitcoin and Ether to Coinbase, a transaction that may reflect portfolio rebalancing or operational custody activity. The transfer stood out as one of the day’s most notable institutional crypto flows.

items.title: Solana prepares validators for Alpenglow upgrade
items.summary: Solana validators are being prepared for the Alpenglow update, which is described as potentially boosting transaction speed by up to 80 times. The rollout is expected to happen in phases from August through October.

items.title: BNB Chain targets 2027 mainnet for new agentic-trading Layer 1
items.summary: BNB Chain is building a new Layer 1 designed for agentic trading, with a planned mainnet launch in 2027. The project signals continued investment in specialized blockchain infrastructure for automated trading use cases.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, marking a push into professional AI tools and workplace automation. The release intensifies competition with other enterprise AI offerings.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time conversations
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The company says the capability is aimed at more natural live conversation and use cases such as live translation.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, making the model available in preview through its developer-facing API. The move places Meta in more direct competition with Anthropic and OpenAI on commercial model access.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4.5, which it described as its most intelligent model to date and optimized for coding and agentic tasks. The launch adds another major frontier-model release to the competitive AI model race.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September as part of a broader effort to expand computing power. The company is aiming to boost overall capacity to 14 gigawatts next year.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the startup aligned with its public mission. The move highlights continued governance and safety focus among frontier AI firms.

items.title: UN digital agency launches initiative to improve trust in AI agents
items.summary: The United Nations agency for digital technologies announced a new initiative focused on improving trust in AI agents. The effort comes as increasingly autonomous systems raise concerns about accountability and human oversight.

items.title: Saudi-backed Humain and Cohere announce AI compute collaboration
items.summary: Saudi Arabia-backed AI company Humain and Cohere said they will collaborate on areas including AI compute. The partnership reflects rising demand for compute capacity and growing international AI alliances.

items.title: Microsoft shifts some products away from OpenAI and Anthropic models
items.summary: Future Tools reported that Microsoft is moving some products from OpenAI and Anthropic models to its own MAI model family in order to cut costs. If confirmed broadly, the shift would signal stronger pressure on model providers as major cloud platforms internalize more AI capability.

items.title: Industry trend: AI infrastructure spending continues to surge
items.summary: Reuters reported major new infrastructure investments tied to AI demand, including Micron's plan to invest more than $250 billion in the U.S. through 2035 and Meta's new data center in Alberta. These moves point to continued scaling of chips, compute, and data center capacity across the industry.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass adds new July 2026 wave, including several upcoming releases
items.summary: Microsoft has revealed the latest wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass in July 2026, continuing its steady cadence of subscription updates. The announcement is one of the day’s main service-related industry stories.

items.title: Xbox layoffs reportedly hit multiple major studios
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft’s latest cuts have significantly affected id Software and Obsidian, adding to the wider industry uncertainty around studio staffing and restructuring. The fallout is also prompting broader questions about Xbox’s internal priorities.

items.title: IO confirms Project Fantasy will continue independently after Xbox split
items.summary: IO Interactive has confirmed that Project Fantasy will move forward on its own, following its separation from Xbox-related plans. The update is notable for both fans of the studio and observers of shifting publishing relationships.

items.title: WayForward teases next Shantae game
items.summary: WayForward announced a new Shantae project at Anime Expo and gave it a 2027 release window. The reveal is one of the clearest new game announcements highlighted in current coverage.

items.title: Pokémon GO marks its 10th anniversary with livestream coverage
items.summary: Pokémon GO is celebrating its 10th anniversary with a special livestream, with live coverage expected to track new announcements and surprises. The event stands out as the main mobile-game news item in the current roundup.

items.title: Mario Kart Tour shutdown date announced
items.summary: Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour in September after seven years of service, marking a notable end for one of its long-running mobile titles. The move is a significant platform and live-service development.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 arrive on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: Activision’s Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 are now available on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. IGN notes that the ports are out now, though they come at a relatively high price.

items.title: GTA Online sets up next major update
items.summary: Rockstar’s next GTA Online update, The Kortz Center Heist, is set to launch next week. The coverage also notes that fans have already spotted Rockstar-related Easter eggs tied to the update.

items.title: DC K.O. announced as new mobile fighting game
items.summary: Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment and Drop Fake announced DC K.O., a new DC mobile fighting game planned for iOS and Android in 2027. Pre-registration is already open.

items.title: Fortnite adds new American Dad crossover bundle
items.summary: Epic Games released a new American Dad crossover bundle in Fortnite’s Item Shop, though fans were disappointed that Roger was not included. The bundle is also notable as another example of Epic’s ongoing licensed-content strategy.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks
items.summary: Global financial messaging network Swift introduced a blockchain-based shared ledger aimed at enabling round-the-clock payments and competing with stablecoin-based systems. The launch includes an initial group of 16 banks such as Citi and HSBC.

items.title: India removes import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on select parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, removing 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower costs for manufacturers including Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion under Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple plans to spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. The deal also includes Broadcom expanding a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans to start manufacturing its own AI chip in September
items.summary: Meta is preparing to begin manufacturing a custom chip from September as part of efforts to expand its computing capacity. An internal memo said the company is targeting substantial growth in overall compute next year.

items.title: MFE-MediaForEurope to launch single streaming platform across Europe
items.summary: MFE-MediaForEurope said it plans to combine technologies from its Italian and German businesses into one streaming platform across its European markets. The move is intended to strengthen its competition with global digital and advertising companies.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules for detecting child sexual abuse material
items.summary: European Union lawmakers supported a proposal to reinstate temporary rules allowing platforms such as Google and Meta to detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The measure affects major online service providers and content moderation practices.

items.title: Microsoft cuts about 3,200 jobs in Xbox restructuring
items.summary: Microsoft is eliminating roughly 3,200 jobs across its Xbox video game business as it restructures the division. The company is shifting resources toward artificial intelligence-related priorities.
